title: Evidence-Led Capacity Experimentation Framework
author: Asha Patel
summary: This document defines a repeatable framework that ties capacity experiments to SLOs and incident evidence. It introduces the Evidence Ledger format, experiment templates, acceptance and rollback criteria, required telemetry, and integration points with our operational tooling. The goal is to move capacity decisions from ad-hoc guesses to evidence-led experiments that can be reviewed as part of post-incident analysis and SLO lifecycle governance.
body:
Overview:

This page describes 'Evidence-Led Capacity Experimentation' — a structured process for running capacity and configuration experiments (scale, batching, cache, quantization, routing) against production-like traffic while ensuring SLOs and error budgets are respected. The framework has three pillars: 1) Observable experiment design, 2) Evidence Ledger, 3) Governance and rollback.

Why this exists:
- We repeatedly see capacity work that is either over-provisioned (wasted spend) or under-provisioned (SLO regressions).
- Experiments that change serving parameters often surface only during incidents because evidence was incomplete.
- Tying experiments to documented evidence reduces surprise and shortens incident reviews.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: model-serving clusters (hosted + dedicated), inference routing policies, autoscale policies, cold/warm pool experiments, batching and KV-cache experiments, quantization profile validation.
- Non-goals: long-term architecture re-architecture proposals (these belong in design docs), one-off exploratory CI tests (those belong in eval-harness).

Definitions (short):
- Experiment: any deliberate change to capacity/configuration that could affect latency, throughput, or correctness.
- Evidence Ledger: a structured artifact that captures telemetry, hypothesis, dataset, and decision rationale for each experiment.
- Acceptance Window: the period and thresholds used to judge experiment success.

Roles and ownership:
- Experiment Owner: leads experiment design, executes, writes Evidence Ledger (typically an SRE or platform engineer).
- Reviewers: 1 product or stack owner + 1 reliability engineer.
- Approver: Service SLO owner (for changes that touch error budget) or Service Steward for low-risk experiments.
- Oncall Liaison: notifies oncall before experiment start when run in production.

Evidence Ledger format (required fields):
- Experiment ID (id-YYYYMMNN-<short>)
- Title (short)
- Hypothesis (one-sentence)
- Impacted services (list of service names)
- SLOs at risk (SLO id and current burn rate)
- Start/End timestamps and Approval token (who approved)
- Traffic pattern and sampling method (e.g., 5% sampled tokens, hashed tenant IDs)
- Metric targets (primary metrics and acceptance criteria)
- Observability dashboard links (Prometheus/Grafana queries)
- Artifact snapshot (git commit, config blob, quantization profile id)
- Rollback triggers and actions
- Post-experiment verdict and notes

Example Evidence Ledger (text table):
Experiment ID: EXP-20260111-kv-cache
Title: "KV prefix cache warm-pool sizing for small-tenant embedding workloads"
Hypothesis: "A warm-pool of 50 warm models will reduce 95th percentile latency by 18% for small tenants without increasing token cost >1%"
Impacted services: model-serve-west, routing-proxy
SLOs at risk: text-generation-95p-latency (99.5% target), embedding-throughput (SLO unaffected)
Traffic pattern: 10% hashed by tenant-id; weekday morning profile replay from synthetic canary
Metric targets (Acceptance Window):
- 95th latency must improve by >= 10% relative to baseline and not regress 99th latency > 2%
- Error rate (HTTP 5xx) must remain within historical mean + 3 sigma

Observability / Required Telemetry:
- Prometheus queries (examples):
  - Baseline 95p latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - Error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))
  - KV cache hit-rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- Traces: Distributed trace sampling = 100% for experiment tag (temporary) for 1 hour, then 10%
- Logs: error-level logs forwarded to short-term retention index with experiment tag

Acceptance and Rollback rules (must be explicit in ledger):
1) Immediate rollback triggers (auto): HTTP 5xx increase > 3x baseline or SLO burn rate increases above threshold (see SLO Burn Trigger table below).
2) Manual rollback triggers: if majority of reviewers observe unexplained tail-latency regressions during acceptance window.
3) Graceful rollback steps: flip routing flag to prior config, drain warm pool with 5-min window, monitor for regressions, close ticket with evidence.

SLO Burn Trigger table (examples to use in ledger):
- Low-risk experiments (0–5% traffic): auto-rollback if burn-rate doubles for two consecutive 5m windows.
- Medium-risk (5–20%): auto-rollback if burn-rate triples or 5xx rate > historical mean + 3 sigma.
- High-risk (>20%): require oncall-liaison and canary runway; auto-rollback if any SLO breach in acceptance window.

Experiment lifecycle (step-by-step):
1) Design phase (Doc): write Evidence Ledger draft, include queries and dashboards. 2) Dry-run: run in staging or canary traffic replay for minimum 2 business-day profile unless experiment is low-risk. 3) Approval: get approver sign-off; record token in ledger. 4) Production ramp: start at configured sample rate, monitor the acceptance window with automated checks. 5) Decision: conclude PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE in ledger with collected artifacts. 6) Postmortem tie-in: if experiment contributed to incident, attach ledger to incident review as canonical evidence.

Operational Tooling integration (how to wire this into our stack):
- Feature flagging: use ffctl to create experiment flag namespaced to service (example CLI):
  - ffctl create model-serve-west/EXP-20260111-kv-cache --initial 0.01 --buckets 0.01,0.05,0.10
- Alerting: create a temporary alert group (label: experiment=EXP-20260111) with the rules from the ledger. Avoid adding permanent alerts for temporary experiments.
- Dashboard template: copy /dashboards/experiment-template and populate variables: service, experiment_id, baseline_period, traffic_sample.
- Evidence storage: upload ledger as a JSON blob to evidence-store (internal API /v1/evidence) and link artifact id in ledger.

Runbook: Quick start (Production sampled experiment):
1) Pre-flight checklist (owner confirms):
   - SLO owner notified (email + slack)
   - Oncall Liaison scheduled (time window)
   - Evidence Ledger draft stored and linked
   - Dashboards and alerts created with experiment=tag
   - Rollback script reviewed and smoke-tested in staging
2) Ramp plan: 1% -> 5% -> 10% (5–10 minutes between steps for low-latency checks); for longer tests use 1h windows at each step.
3) Acceptance checks at each step (automated):
   - 95p latency change < -10% or within -/+2% of baseline as allowed by ledger
   - Error rate within defined delta
   - Latency distribution skew unchanged or improved
4) If auto-rollback condition triggers, run the rollback script and notify the #sre-experiments channel with ledger id.
5) After experiment end, archive telemetry with tag experiment_id and set retention to 90 days for full fidelity evidence.

Incident review standards (how experiment evidence is used in postmortems):
- Attach the Evidence Ledger as a primary artifact. The post-incident template must include a section: "Experiment interaction analysis" describing whether experiment overlapped incident window and referencing metric deltas.
- If experiment caused or amplified incident, the Incident Severity owner will require: 1) hold on similar experiments for 72 hours, 2) remediation plan entry, 3) change to approval policy for that experiment class.

Templates and artifacts (copy/paste friendly):
- Rollback CLI snippet (shell):
  - # flip routing flag back
  - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://ops-api.internal/v1/flags/model-serve-west/EXP-20260111/rollback"
- Prometheus alert example (YAML snippet):
  - alert: EXP-20260111-High5xx
    expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="model-serve-west", code=~"5..", experiment="EXP-20260111"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="model-serve-west", experiment="EXP-20260111"}[5m]))) > 0.01
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "Experiment EXP-20260111 5xx rate > 1%"

Compliance and auditability:
- All experiments that touch an SLO must have an Evidence Ledger that is retained for 1 year and attached to the SLO governance board entry.
- Access control: only members of eng-sre or eng-platform can approve medium and high-risk experiments.

Metrics and KPIs to monitor framework success (quarterly review):
- Fraction of capacity changes that used Evidence Ledger before rollout (target >= 90%).
- Incidents where experiment evidence was sufficient for causal determination (target >= 80%).
- Mean time from experiment start to decision (target <= 4 hours for low-risk runs).
- Cost delta discovered and realized by optimization experiments (dollar savings tracked per quarter).

Appendices:
A. Example experiment ticket template (Jira title and fields):
- Title: EXP-20260111 - KV cache warm pool sizing
- Epic/Service: model-serve-west
- Priority: Normal
- Experiment ID: EXP-20260111
- Evidence Ledger: link
- Start window: 2026-01-20T09:00Z
- Rollback runbook: link

B. Frequently asked questions (short):
- Q: Can experiments run outside business hours?
  A: Yes, but medium/high-risk experiments require oncall-liaison coverage during the acceptance window.
- Q: Who signs approvals for quantization profile changes?
  A: Quantization changes that affect model quality must be co-signed by Research/Applied ML and Service SLO owner.

C. Change log (summary):
- 2026-01-11: initial publish (Asha Patel)
- 2026-02-03: added Prometheus examples and clarified auto-rollback thresholds (A. Patel, M. Rivera)

End of document.
